paper.title_en: Equilibrium baseline for transverse-momentum correlations in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 3$-$39$ GeV: Conservation laws, resonance decays, quantum statistics, and collective flow
paper.abstract_en: Event-by-event transverse-momentum correlations measured by STAR in Au+Au collisions exhibit a nonmonotonic energy dependence with a minimum near $\sqrt{s_{NN}} \approx 5$-$8$ GeV and a steep rise toward $3$ GeV. Before interpreting these features in terms of a softened equation of state or a QCD critical point, the baseline from an equilibrated hadron resonance gas must be established. Here we compute the two-particle correlator $\langle Δp_{T,i}Δp_{T,j} \rangle$ in thermal and chemical equilibrium from $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 3$ to $39$ GeV for 0-5% and 30-40% collisions, incorporating resonance decays, Bose-Einstein statistics, Bjorken longitudinal and transverse radial flow, and global conservation of energy, baryon number, electric charge, strangeness, and transverse momentum. Imposing conservation laws via a saddle-point expansion of the microcanonical ensemble yields the variance of any additive observable as a Schur complement of grand-canonical covariances. Although the equilibrium gas undergoes the transition from baryon- to meson-dominated matter, composition fluctuations cancel the large negative "mixing" term that arises when species multiplicities are fixed event by event, leaving only a much smaller negative conservation residual. Across $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 11.5$-$39$ GeV, the equilibrium baseline with strong flow underpredicts the data by a factor of $3$-$4$ in 0-5% and $\approx 6.5$ in 30-40% collisions; at fixed-target energies ($3$-$5.2$ GeV), where the data are largest and positive, the baseline turns negative. Accounting for the data via radial-flow fluctuations at fixed energy requires $σ_β/β_s \approx 6$-$10\%$ in central and $\approx 22\%$ in 30-40% collider-energy collisions, growing faster with decreasing centrality than independent-source scaling.
